assessment.nobel_worthiness: The heterogeneous-firm trade framework changed how economists understand selection, reallocation and the gains from trade. It also shaped a large body of empirical work using firm-level data. It extends the earlier trade-theory recognition from 2008 and carries wide influence across fields.
assessment.attribution: Melitz's 2003 model is the central contribution. Helpman's work with Melitz and Yeaple on exporting versus FDI, and his broader theoretical program, gives a strong second credit. Redding's quantitative spatial and trade work is important but later and more separable, so I leave him off this proposal.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of confirmation, replication and extension. The core predictions have been tested repeatedly across countries and datasets. The timing is ripe.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers Melitz alone or a pairing with Helpman, and how it would treat Melitz-Chaney and Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum antecedents that are not credited on this list.
Quantitative magnitudes of the gains from trade in heterogeneous-firm models are debated, and those debates may weigh on how the contribution is characterised.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Task-based accounts of technological change, together with the China-shock evidence on local labour-market adjustment, changed the understanding of inequality, polarisation, trade and the persistence of regional damage. Both lines are highly policy-relevant and speak to current debates on automation and AI.
assessment.attribution: Autor is the common thread across both lines. Hanson and Dorn are central to the trade-shock evidence. Katz's earlier work on skill demand matters, but he overlaps with other candidate groupings. Acemoglu and Restrepo, who developed the task framework further, are not on this list, which complicates credit for the task-based theory.
assessment.maturity: The China-shock work is now over a decade old and has been extensively replicated and debated. The underlying empirical design has been refined in response to critiques. It is mature enough for recognition.
uncertainties: The task-model attribution is incomplete without the Acemoglu-Restrepo theoretical contributions.
Exposure-design identification and the long-run size of the effects continue to be debated.
Which framing, trade shocks or technology, the committee would choose is unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The collateral-constraint model of credit cycles explains how small shocks are amplified and persist through asset prices and borrowing limits. It is foundational for macro-finance, for the post-2008 literature and for central-bank thinking about financial stability.
assessment.attribution: The 1997 Kiyotaki-Moore paper is the clearly identifiable origin and gives a tight two-person credit. Gertler and Gilchrist are important for the financial accelerator and its empirical side, but Bernanke already received the 2022 prize for related work, and their inclusion would dilute the core.
assessment.maturity: Almost three decades old, with extensive follow-up. The theory is embedded in standard macro-financial models. Timing is mature, and the post-crisis literature has reinforced its relevance.
uncertainties: The committee may want an empirical anchor alongside the theory.
The relation to the 2022 financial-intermediation prize could be read as either complementary or redundant.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Systematic formal and empirical analysis of how constitutions, electoral rules and state capacity shape fiscal policy and development. It created modern political economics as a field of economics and has strong links to the institutions-and-growth recognition of 2024.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini are the core of the constitutional and electoral-rules work. Besley is central on state capacity and political accountability. The trio is coherent, though the field has many contributors beyond these names.
assessment.maturity: Decades of cumulative work, a standard textbook and a large empirical literature. It is mature, but a recent institutions prize may reduce urgency.
uncertainties: Persson's past association with the prize-awarding process is a disclosed conflict that is not adjudicated here.
The 2024 institutions prize may be seen as having already covered adjacent ground.
Causal identification in cross-country constitutional comparisons is contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-run historical series of top incomes and wealth, built from tax and archival records, reshaped the empirical and public debate on inequality. The method is a major data-construction contribution and relevant to long-run economic history.
assessment.attribution: Piketty and Saez built the foundational top-income series and the analysis of its dynamics. Zucman's contributions on offshore wealth and distributional national accounts are newer and more separable. Credit is spread across a large collaborative World Inequality Database network.
assessment.maturity: The core top-income work dates from the early 2000s and has been widely replicated and extended. Some interpretive claims, such as the r>g mechanism, remain contested, but the measurement contribution is established.
uncertainties: Theoretical claims in the later work are disputed.
Measurement choices, such as tax-unit definitions and treatment of capital income, affect findings.
Overlap with the public-economics candidate involving Saez complicates credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The structural estimation of demand with differentiated products and of dynamic industry models gave empirical industrial organisation its modern toolkit. It is used in merger analysis, antitrust and regulation worldwide, and it combines theory with real data.
assessment.attribution: The BLP framework (Berry, Levinsohn, Pakes) is a clearly identifiable joint contribution. Pakes also has the dynamic-games work, with Ericson and others. Bresnahan's earlier work is important but on a list of seven names, credit is diffuse.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of use. The methods are standard and well tested, so timing is not a concern.
uncertainties: Credit may be thought too technical or too narrow relative to other candidates.
Identification and computational issues in BLP and dynamic-game estimators are continuing topics of debate.
The set of credited names is large, so the three-person cut is a judgement.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Heterogeneous-agent New Keynesian models changed the analysis of monetary and fiscal transmission by showing the importance of household balance sheets, marginal propensities to consume and distribution. This is highly influential in current policy work.
assessment.attribution: The Kaplan-Moll-Violante framework is clearly credited as a trio. It builds on earlier incomplete-markets work by others, which would need acknowledgement in any assessment.
assessment.maturity: Roughly a decade old. It is influential, but long-run empirical validation and consolidation are still under way. This is probably somewhat early for the prize.
uncertainties: Maturity: the models are still being tested against data and their policy implications are not settled.
Credit relative to the earlier heterogeneous-agent macro literature may be questioned.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification put the question of what can be learned under weak assumptions at the centre of empirical practice. It supports more transparent inference and improved credibility, with applications in many applied fields.
assessment.attribution: Manski is the originator of the approach. Tamer made key contributions to inference and econometric theory for partially identified models. Molinari has made important later contributions, but the pairing gives a cleaner credit line.
assessment.maturity: Decades old at the foundation. The statistical machinery for inference has developed more recently. Recognition has historically been more readily given to methods with widely used applications.
uncertainties: Adoption in applied work is narrower than for other econometric methods.
The committee may judge the methodological contribution relative to the substantive-discovery candidates differently across fields.
Whether to reward foundations (Manski) or inference theory (Tamer, Molinari) is uncertain.
